result.reason: The passage covers exactly what candidate 9 ('Ve-hikrivo Question') discusses: the Tanna Kamma's need for ve-hikrivo given his derivation from u-malak ve-hiktir, followed by the answer that without ve-hikrivo one might have read kemishpat as comparing to chatat ha-of (candidate 10) or read u-malak ve-hiktir as teaching melikah at the top of the mizbeach (candidate 11) — all of which is one continuous chain of question and answer belonging under the Ve-hikrivo Question heading, not the current placement under 'Ve-hikrivo Response' (index 7) which addresses Rabbi Elazar b'Rabbi Shimon's position.

The passage directly quotes Rav Ḥisda's derivation from the verse 'And Aaron shall sacrifice the bull of the sin offering that is his' to teach that it must come from his own resources, not communal or tithe property — which matches exactly what the 'Aaron's Offering' section's prose describes.

The passage directly discusses how the daytime requirement for the bird burnt offering is derived from the verse 'bayom tzivoso' rather than from the animal sin offering comparison, and the Gemara's conclusion that it was cited 'kedi nasba' (incidentally) — which is precisely what the 'Daytime Requirement' prose section describes.

Both items together present the objection (right hand is derived from Rabba bar bar Ḥana's rule about etzba or kehuna) and the response (the first Tanna holds kehuna requires etzba too, so the rule doesn't apply alone), which is precisely the 'Finger vs Kohen' refinement described in candidate 1's prose about kehuna ba'ia etzba.

The passage directly addresses the question of how the Tanna Kamma and Rabbi Elazar b'Rabbi Shimon know that melikah is performed from the back of the neck, which is precisely what the prose under 'Melikah Location' (index 2) poses as its question.

All nine items deal exclusively with the age requirements for turtledoves (torim) and young pigeons (bnei yonah) — which stage is fit or unfit for each, the biblical derivations, and the intermediate yellowing stage — precisely the content described in the 'Age Requirement' prose.

Both items together form Rava's argument from the baraita — Item 1 is Rabbi Zeira's dilemma (the setup) and Item 2 is Rava's attempt to resolve it via the verse excluding techilat ha-tzihuya — which matches exactly the prose of candidate 13 ('Rava's Argument'), not the current placement under 'Golden Feathers' which only describes the mishna's basic ruling about the yellowing stage.

The passage states exactly that the verse was needed to exclude nirva and ne'evad (bestiality/idolatry cases), which is the precise content the 'Asmachta Response' prose describes as the Gemara's rejection of Rava's proof.
